item.title: How Will Ethiopia’s New Stock Market Impact Local Investors?
item.description: Ethiopia has launched its first stock exchange, aiming to modernize its economy. But with low internet access, limited financial literacy, and public distrust in finance, will everyday Ethiopians be able to take part?

item.title: Fintech in Francophone Africa: What’s Driving Growth and What’s Holding It Back
item.description: Explore the growth of fintech startups in Francophone West Africa, including Côte d’Ivoire and Senegal. This article covers key challenges, regulatory changes, and insights from MagmaSend on scaling across the WAEMU region.

item.title: Why Intra-African Flights Are So Expensive (And What Could Change)
item.description: Intra-African flights often cost more than flying to Europe or Asia. Learn why airfares within Africa remain so high, the structural challenges behind them, and what solutions like SAATM could mean for the future of affordable air travel.

item.title: How Latin America Is Rewiring Money with Stablecoins and Pix
item.description: Stablecoins, Pix, and SPEI are building Latin America’s new payment infrastructure—faster, cheaper, and locally powered.

item.title: Why Ride-Sharing Giants Struggle to Crack Brazil
item.description: Brazil is one of the biggest ride-sharing markets in the world — and one of the hardest to win. In this episode of Emerging Markets Today, Luiz Fittipaldi (ex-Bolt) explains why global players like Uber and Didi struggle to crack the market, how Pix changed payments, and why tier-2 and tier-3 cities are the next frontier.

item.title: Brazil: What It Takes to Break Into the Ride-Sharing Market
item.description: Former Bolt strategist Luiz Fittipaldi explains why Brazil’s ride-sharing market is so complex — from regulation and Pix to São Paulo traffic and new growth frontiers.

item.title: Uber Safari’s High Price and Low Transparency Raise Questions in Kenya
item.description: Uber Safari launched in Nairobi National Park with a promise of accessibility. But its premium price, lack of transparency on vehicle standards, and growing public skepticism are raising questions about who really benefits from this service.
